subject: Mathematics
title: Logarithms
learningOutcomes: Express a number in scientific notation and convert scientific notation back to ordinary form.
Describe the logarithm of a number and convert between logarithmic form and exponential form.
Differentiate between the common logarithm (base 10) and the natural logarithm (base e).
Find the characteristic and the mantissa of a common logarithm.
Find the logarithm and the antilogarithm of a number using the log and antilog tables.
State and use the laws of logarithms: product, quotient, power and change of base.
Expand, simplify and write expressions as a single logarithm; solve simple logarithmic equations.
Use logarithm tables to evaluate products, quotients, powers and roots, and solve real-life problems.

sections.heading: Scientific Notation
sections.body: A number written as \(a\times10^{n}\) with \(1\le a<10\) and \(n\) an integer is in scientific notation. Move the decimal point to just after the first non-zero digit; the number of places moved is \(n\) (positive if you moved left, negative if you moved right). Example: \(45000=4.5\times10^{4}\) and \(0.00032=3.2\times10^{-4}\).

sections.heading: Meaning of a Logarithm
sections.body: A logarithm is a power. If \(a^{x}=y\) (with \(a>0,\ a\ne1,\ y>0\)) then \(\log_{a}y=x\). The base stays the base, the power becomes the answer. Special values: \(\log_{a}1=0\) and \(\log_{a}a=1\). Logarithms of zero and of negative numbers are not defined.

sections.heading: Common and Natural Logarithms
sections.body: Logarithms to base 10 are common logarithms; \(\log N\) means \(\log_{10}N\). Logarithms to base \(e\approx2.718\) are natural logarithms, written \(\ln N\). They are connected by \(\ln N=2.3026\log N\).

sections.heading: Characteristic and Mantissa
sections.body: Every common logarithm is written as characteristic + mantissa: the characteristic is the integer part and the mantissa is a positive decimal part (\(0\le\) mantissa \(<1\)). For \(N\ge1\): characteristic = (number of digits before the decimal point) \(-1\). For \(0<N<1\): characteristic = \(-(\text{zeros after the point}+1)\), written in bar notation, e.g. \(\bar{3}\). The mantissa depends only on the digits, not on the decimal point.

sections.heading: Reading the Log Table
sections.body: Ignore the decimal point and take four digits. The first two digits choose the row, the third digit the column, and the fourth digit the mean-difference column; add the mean difference to the column value to get the mantissa. Then add the characteristic. Example: \(\log 13.45\): digits 1345 ⇒ row 13, column 4 gives 1271, mean difference for 5 adds 16, mantissa 0.1287; characteristic 1; so \(\log 13.45=1.1287\).

sections.heading: Antilogarithm
sections.body: The antilogarithm undoes the logarithm: if \(\log N=x\) then \(N=\text{antilog}\,x\). Use the mantissa to read four digits from the antilog table (row = first two decimal digits, column = third, mean difference = fourth), then place the decimal point using the characteristic: characteristic \(c\ge0\) gives \(c+1\) digits before the point; \(\bar{k}\) gives \(k-1\) zeros after the point.

sections.heading: Laws of Logarithms
sections.body: Product law: \(\log_{a}(mn)=\log_{a}m+\log_{a}n\). Quotient law: \(\log_{a}\frac{m}{n}=\log_{a}m-\log_{a}n\). Power law: \(\log_{a}m^{n}=n\log_{a}m\). Change of base: \(\log_{b}m=\frac{\log_{a}m}{\log_{a}b}\). There is no law for \(\log(m+n)\).

sections.heading: Calculations Using Logarithms
sections.body: To multiply, ADD the logs; to divide, SUBTRACT the logs; to find a power \(N^{k}\), MULTIPLY \(\log N\) by \(k\); to find a root, DIVIDE \(\log N\) by the index. Always finish by taking the antilog of the result.

sections.heading: Logarithmic Equations
sections.body: Convert to exponential form: \(\log_{a}x=k\Rightarrow x=a^{k}\). If several logs appear, combine them with the laws first (single log on each side), then remove the log. Reject any solution that makes an argument of a log zero or negative.

definitions.definition: A number written as \(a\times10^{n}\) with \(1\le a<10\) and \(n\) an integer.
If \(a^{x}=y\) then \(x\) is the logarithm of \(y\) to base \(a\), written \(\log_{a}y=x\).
The number \(a\) in \(\log_{a}y\); it must be positive and not equal to 1.
A logarithm to base 10, written \(\log N\).
A logarithm to base \(e\) (\(e\approx2.718\)), written \(\ln N\).
The integral part of a common logarithm.
The positive decimal part of a common logarithm (between 0 and 1).
A way of writing a negative characteristic with a positive mantissa, e.g. \(\bar{2}.5563\) means \(-2+0.5563\).
The number whose logarithm is given: if \(\log N=x\) then \(N=\text{antilog}\,x\).
The extra columns of the table used for the fourth digit of a number or mantissa.

examTips: Always write the base and keep the order: \(a^{x}=y\Leftrightarrow\log_{a}y=x\) (the base stays the base).
Characteristic of \(N\ge1\) = digits before the point \(-1\); for \(N<1\) it is \(-(\text{zeros after the point}+1)\), written with a bar.
The mantissa depends only on the digits. 345.6 and 0.003456 have the same mantissa but different characteristics.
In the log table use Row (first 2 digits) \(\to\) Column (3rd digit) \(\to\) Mean difference (4th digit) and ADD the mean difference.
Multiply \(\Rightarrow\) add logs; divide \(\Rightarrow\) subtract logs; power \(\Rightarrow\) multiply the log; root \(\Rightarrow\) divide the log.
With bar numbers, add or subtract the characteristics separately from the mantissas and carry any whole number.
There is no law for \(\log(m+n)\) or \(\log(m-n)\): do not split sums or differences.
In a log equation, check that every argument is positive; reject answers that make one zero or negative.
Table answers are 4-figure approximations: the last digit may differ by 1 from a calculator.
